Consult your local AEA for advice on the recommended fall army worm control pesticide in your area (APNI). Check your maize field at least once a week for unusual patterns like insect damage, larvae, or stunted growth. To reduce future Fall Armyworm infestations, rotate maize with non-host plants like groundnut, deep plough, or burn infested residues, and keep the field well-weeded.

This advice comes from guides for Northern Ghana and may not suit Kintampo, so check the timing with your local extension agent. Consult your local AEA for advice on the recommended fall army worm control pesticide in your area (APNI). To manage Fall Armyworm in your maize, rotate crops with groundnut. Deep plough, bury, or burn infested maize residues. Keep your field well-weeded. Check your field at least once a week for signs of infestation. Ask your local Agricultural Extension Agent for advice on recommended pesticides to control Fall Armyworm.

Planting Window: The major season transition period is either from mid-March to end of April  or from end of March to end of April. The minor season transition period is either from mid-July through August to early September  or from mid-July to early September. Planting Time: Plant after three good rains within the planting window to ensure enough soil moisture. Sow after the rains have stabilized to avoid wilting. Your extension officer will confirm which to follow.

Top dressing should be done when the soil is moist, to enhance the dissolving of applied nutrients in the soil as this allows for faster uptake of nutrients. If at 6 weeks after planting maize the soil is very dry, delay the topdress fertilizer application until some rains are received. The first fertilizer application (basal application) should be applied shortly after germination at about two weeks after planting. The Right time for application of top-dressing fertilizer is at 6 weeks after planting.
